_doc: SHARED FIXTURES for the MAPS · Data Center Theme map-state policy (dc-map-state@1).
ONE file, read by BOTH halves of the policy, because the policy is expressed twice:
Two implementations of one rule is how the two halves drift apart, and a drift here is
invisible: the browser would block an approval the server allows, or the reverse. So
test/maps-dc-policy-parity.test.mjs runs the JS validator over every case offline, and —
when database credentials are present — sends the identical cases to the SQL guard and
requires the SAME verdict on every one. Adding a case here adds it to both sides at once.
`expect_governed` is the SCOPE question (does this policy apply to this row at all) and
`expect_ok` is the VERDICT. They are separate on purpose: a row the policy does not
govern must produce NO violations, which is a different fact from a compliant capture.
The evidence shape is taken verbatim from the live Mesa draft 78ee8931-c114-4824-9a29-
cannot drift into a shape the queue does not carry.

`project` names which project block a case is built from — `project` (the Mesa data centre) by default, or `ordinary_project` for the non-data-centre scope control. A fixture whose 'ordinary' row still classified as a data centre would test nothing.
